summary: This resolution allows House consideration of the FY2026 Department of Homeland Security appropriations bill by waiving all points of order, deeming the bill read, limiting debate to one hour equally divided between the parties, and permitting one motion to recommit before final passage.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural, enabling floor consideration of an appropriations bill for DHS. It contains no language that sets, increases, or decreases any spending levels, nor does it direct policy on overall government expenditures. Therefore it has no bearing on government spending.
The resolution text addresses only House procedure for an appropriations measure and makes no reference to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No provisions in the resolution relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market-based reforms.
The resolution contains no language concerning firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

While the underlying bill (H.R. 7744) appropriates funds for DHS, which administers immigration and border functions, the resolution itself is strictly procedural and does not engage with immigration policy, enforcement levels, or pathways.
No mention of reproductive health services, funding restrictions, or access issues appears in the resolution.

DHS appropriations can include some homeland-security functions that overlap with defense, but the resolution text itself makes no substantive changes or statements about military or defense spending.
The resolution does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or related funding.
No provisions touch on welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net funding.
The resolution is silent on education policy, school funding, or choice programs.
No content relates to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related appropriations.
The resolution does not engage with sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
Although the underlying measure involves appropriations (which affect deficits), the resolution itself contains no statements or directives on debt reduction versus deficit spending.
The resolution makes no reference to LGBTQ protections or related civil-rights issues.
No foreign-aid provisions appear in the text.
The resolution addresses only legislative procedure for an appropriations bill and does not touch on voting access or election integrity.
No language concerns technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance authorities.
The resolution does not address labor rights, union powers, or employer flexibility.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
